key_insight: The paper replaces hard, deterministic droplet-collision regime boundaries with a probabilistic, symbolic analytical model that captures smooth transitions between outcomes.
engineering_relevance: This gives spray-simulation engineers a practical collision submodel that is both physically interpretable and better suited to high-pressure, Eulerian-Lagrangian calculations.
method: Trained a machine-learning teacher on ~40,000 experimental collision events across 8 regimes and 5 dimensionless parameters.
Used symbolic regression to distill the learned probability field into 8 class-specific analytical expressions.
Implemented a “biased-dice” sampling scheme to draw collision outcomes consistently in simulation.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated against conventional analytical boundary models and, using over 5,000 high-pressure data points up to 50 atm, it performed better while reproducing gradual probability transitions.
watch_item: The biased-dice implementation must be integrated carefully so the probabilistic sampling remains statistically consistent with the intended collision probabilities.
paper_title: Probabilistic Symbolic-Distillation Model of Droplet Collision for Spray Simulation at High Ambient Pressures
